Senses.Explanation: Gradual cultivation is work that proceeds by stages rather than being completed at once. Guifeng Zongmi says it means that afflictions, causal conduct, and resulting qualities remain unfinished. Yongming Yanshou places it both in a gradual-cultivation/sudden-realization sequence and among paths that mature through successive stages. The records therefore do not make it one fixed sequence; they use it to distinguish progressive maturation from the sudden member of several paired classifications.
Senses.Note: Literally cultivation carried out gradually. The retained records use it in classifications that set gradual and sudden realization or cultivation in different orders.
